summary.intent: Upgrade the Callisto release tooling from 0.16.0 to 0.17.0 in the caliper repo, then keep progressing other parallel work (trail 172 measurements, crate-wide missing_docs lint, ADR notes) while PRs await review.
summary.outcome: A worker prepared and verified the Callisto 0.17.0 upgrade (commit 6568f816); it was pushed as PR #319 linked to trail 158 and left unmerged pending release runs. Several earlier PRs (#312, #314-#317) merged, and four new workers were started on #318 conflict fixing, layer-only-props measurement, deny-missing-docs/ADR, and the storybook accuracy headline.

repo: Callisto pins in workflows use the full commit SHA of the annotated tag's target (ff116694 for 0.17.0, dec5841b for 0.16.0), not the tag object SHA.
Callisto version appears in .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml (6 setup-callisto + 1 callisto-action pins), .github/workflows/ci.yml, callisto.toml header comment, and docs/releasing.md.
Fixed groups cli-and-npm-wrapper and napi-and-binding require each member to have its own changelog section per release (crates/cli, packages/cli, crates/binding, packages/napi).
Callisto 0.17.0 makes `status --check --strict` fail on the same warnings as `version --strict`; the repo has no warnings so ci.yml now uses --strict.
RELEASE_COORDINATOR_WORKFLOW_PATH remains .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml, which docs/releasing.md relies on for attestation signer verification.
CI/docs-only changes do not need a changeset in this repo.
Weekly alert policy for storybook accuracy: open issues on wrong >0.1% (or rising), silent-wrong agent answer, or budget breach (<2 s, 600 MiB per corpus); time/memory drift no longer opens issues.
workflow: Verify a tool upgrade by downloading both old and new prebuilt binaries, attestation-verifying them (gh attestation verify --signer-workflow ... --deny-self-hosted-runners), and diffing outputs on the real repo state.
Don't merge CI tooling version changes while release runs or a backfill are in flight, to avoid swapping tool versions mid-release.
Workers run in isolated worktrees and are instructed not to push, open PRs, or merge; the coordinating agent pushes and links PRs to trails.
Stacked measurement branches (e.g. measure/layer-only-props on #318) can proceed without resolver changes since they only measure and propose.
